Destination Overview

A city of beautiful contradictions

Tokyo is a city of contrasts — a place where centuries-old shrines sit in the shadow of soaring skyscrapers, where Michelin-starred sushi bars share streets with bustling ramen stalls, and where cutting-edge technology coexists with deeply rooted tradition. With 14 million residents, the world's largest metropolitan area offers endless discovery.

  • 38,000+ temples & shrines
  • More Michelin stars than any city on Earth
  • Bullet trains at 200mph
  • Cherry blossom season (late March)
  • Global capital of gaming & anime
  • Shopping districts for every style

Local Tips

Insider Tips from Our Travel Experts

  1. Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card for seamless subway and convenience store payments

  2. Avoid rush hour (7:30–9:30 AM) on the subway — it's extremely crowded

  3. Slurping noodles is polite — it shows you're enjoying the meal

  4. 7-Eleven and Lawson convenience stores have surprisingly excellent food

  5. Wear slip-on shoes — you'll remove them frequently at temples and restaurants

  6. Rent a pocket WiFi at the airport — coverage is fast and reliable everywhere

  7. Public trash cans are rare — carry a small bag for your waste

  8. Japan is still very cash-based — carry yen, especially outside tourist areas
